damage/scc-base.title: SCC base damage factor lookup

damage/caustic-escalation.title: Caustic cracking time escalation

damage/lining-adjust.title: Lining condition and monitoring adjustment

level1/toxic-area.title: Ammonia/chlorine toxic consequence area

level1/hf-h2s-toxic-coefficients.title: HF/H2S native toxic log-correlation coefficients

level1/hf-h2s-toxic-area.title: HF/H2S duration-dependent toxic consequence area

Positive instantaneous HF mass requires qualified intercept override because printed33,606 is unresolved. No extrapolation or automatic spray/IDLH credit.

level1/misc-toxic-coefficients.title: Miscellaneous continuous toxic SI coefficients
limitations: Ten chemicals, printed SI kg/s and m2 coefficients. Exact printed duration nodes only. AlCl3 powder uses gas-column coefficients for all positive durations per §4.9.8. N/A cells never become zero. Uses SI table directly rather than guessing inconsistent US punctuation/exponents or reconverting US coefficients.

level1/misc-toxic-area.title: Ten additional chemical continuous toxic consequence areas
limitations: Continuous only; no invented instantaneous correlation. Printed SI coefficients used directly; no additional unit conversion. N/A cells block interpolation that touches them. AlCl3 powder is duration-independent for positive duration. Caller qualifies phase and nonignition probability; no automatic spray credit.

level1/toxic-cutoff.title: Historical Level1 toxic concentration screening
limitations: 2016 printed IDLH values: HF30,H2S100,NH3 300,Cl10ppm. Stored-fluid concentration must be on matching IDLH ppm basis, not silently inferred from mass fraction. At or below cutoff evaluation is not required by this source rule. Not a current occupational exposure limit or an atmospheric dispersion safety claim.

level1/toxic-mitigation.title: Apply explicit toxic source mitigation credits
limitations: Owner-qualified reductions only; no fixed default water-spray efficiency. Rate/duration apply to continuous release, mass to instantaneous. These are not the flammable Table4.6 detection magnitude credit. The caller controls the explicit credit basis and avoids applying the same measure twice.

level1/toxic-component-consequence.title: Compose toxic source/duration/mitigation and per-component area
limitations: Single toxic component; mixture maximum and four-hole aggregation are separate. Uses theoretical total leak rate without flammable magnitude reduction. HF/H2S/NH3/Cl use gas/vapor exposure assumptions; miscellaneous phases follow Table4.13. Optional printed IDLH screening only supports four refinery toxins. All interpolation domains and HF ambiguity still apply; mitigation may shorten duration below a supported table range and then evaluation is rejected.

level1/toxic-mixture-consequence.title: Largest individual Level 1 toxic consequence area for a mixture
limitations: Takes already calculated individual toxic component areas and returns the largest; it does not add overlapping clouds, recalculate species release rates, or perform dispersion. For four-hole weighting use the separate hole-weighted/Level 2 composition API.

level1/toxic-hole-summary.title: Four-hole GFF-weighted Level 1 toxic consequence
limitations: Requires one case for each canonical hole. Within each hole the largest individual toxic-component area is used, then areas are weighted by the supplied generic failure frequencies. Detection/DF-adjusted frequencies, dispersion and financial risk are outside this consequence-area API.

level1/flammable-coefficients.title: SI flammable consequence coefficients

release/detection-reduction.title: Detection/isolation reduction factor

release/detection-duration.title: Detection/isolation maximum duration

level1/release-phase.title: Level 1 final consequence phase

level1/energy-efficiency.title: Instantaneous energy efficiency correction

level1/blending-factors.title: Type 0 release/AIT blending factors

level1/flammable-area.title: Type 0 per-hole blended flammable consequence

level1/release-to-flammable.title: Compose source, inventory, controls and per-hole flammable area

level1/release-to-acid.title: Compose controlled release and ACID splash consequence

level1/release-to-toxic.title: Compose controlled release and Level 1 toxic consequence

level1/consequence-summary.title: Four-hole mechanism-weighted final consequence areas

Source STEP 13 references Tables 5.6/5.7, which do not identify prior/conditional probability tables. This implementation explicitly adopts general-thinning Tables 4.5/4.6, consistent with external-corrosion methodology; this interpretation requires independent engineering verification.

damage/external-clscc-base-susceptibilit.title: External/CUI CLSCC climate-temperature base susceptibility
limitations: Eligible austenitic material/service required. CUI complexity/condition/chloride adjustments not included. Source rows overlap at 93 C, requiring manual classification.

damage/external-clscc.title: External chloride SCC damage factor
limitations: Qualified susceptibility and inspection age supplied; eligible material/service screening is separate. External severity scale differs from internal CLSCC.

damage/cui-clscc.title: Chloride SCC under insulation damage factor
limitations: Caller supplies susceptibility AFTER complexity, insulation-condition and chloride adjustments. Eligible material/service screening remains separate.

damage/fatigue-base.title: Piping mechanical fatigue base factor
limitations: Piping only; caller selects vibration/duration band. Source gives no explicit duration factor above 52 weeks or unique numeric classification at 13 weeks.

damage/fatigue-adjustments.title: Piping mechanical fatigue adjustment factors
limitations: Primitive or utility calculation with no additional clause-specific limitation; caller must qualify API 581 applicability, input basis and engineering use.

damage/mechanical-fatigue.title: Piping mechanical fatigue damage factor
limitations: Piping only; qualitative categories supplied by caller. Not a stress-range/cycle-count fatigue life or FFS calculation.

properties/hydrogen-partial-pressure.title: Hydrogen ideal-mixture partial pressure
limitations: Mole fraction times total absolute pressure; not a fugacity model.

damage/htha-factor.title: HTHA susceptibility damage factor
limitations: Qualified susceptibility supplied; historical exposure and pre-1970 fabrication may require more conservative owner review.

damage/htha-carbon-screen.title: Carbon/C-half-Mo HTHA screening and factor
limitations: Current material must match material_group. Uses printed SI 177 C and 0.345 MPa thresholds. Mixed high/low temperature-pressure cases are not assigned by the printed carbon-steel rules and require engineering review. Cr-Mo/API 941 curve screening is separate.

damage/brittle-reference-temperature.title: Brittle fracture reference temperature
limitations: Caller qualifies material and assigns ASME exemption curve. Uses the printed US Table 20.3 (ksi, F), explicitly converted to Pa and K; not rounded SI Table 20.3M. Linear interpolation is a caller-selected engineering interpolation; no extrapolation.

damage/brittle-service-factor.title: Brittle fracture service-experience adjustment

stable_conditions_no_more_severe_future.title: Stable Conditions No More Severe Future

cyclic_fatigue_or_vibration_design_servi.title: Cyclic Fatigue Or Vibration Design Service

limitations: Owner qualifies code compliance, operating history and service exclusions. Thin-component criterion is an independent OR; all eight service criteria are otherwise required. Printed SI thresholds are used.

damage/brittle-base.title: Brittle fracture base damage table
limitations: Printed SI grid: thickness 6.4-101.6 mm and CET-Tref -56 to 56 K. Linear mode is caller-selected bilinear interpolation of DF, not log DF. No extrapolation or service credit applied here.

damage/brittle-fracture.title: Brittle fracture reference/base/service calculation

stable_conditions_no_more_severe_future.title: Stable Conditions No More Severe Future

cyclic_fatigue_or_vibration_design_servi.title: Cyclic Fatigue Or Vibration Design Service

limitations: Caller establishes applicability, ASME curve and CET (including credited controls) per API 579. No inspection credit. Uses US reference-temperature table converted to SI plus printed SI base-DF tables. Caller selects interpolation separately for yield and base-DF grids; no extrapolation.

damage/embrittlement-885f.title: 885 F embrittlement damage factor
limitations: Qualified susceptible ferritic material and evaluation temperature supplied by caller; no inspection credit. Default reference is printed 28 C (301.15 K), which is not the exact conversion of printed 80 F. Uses printed SI delta-temperature rows. Above +56 K DF=0; at +56 K DF=2. Below -56 K rejected. Linear interpolation is an explicit caller choice.

damage/sigma-content.title: Sigma-phase content category
limitations: Content >1% is tabulated: low >1 to <5%, medium >=5 to <10%, high >=10%. At or below 1% the printed categories are unresolved and rejected; no assumed zero DF.

damage/sigma-embrittlement.title: Sigma-phase embrittlement damage factor
limitations: Qualified sigmatized austenitic stainless steel and content category supplied. No automatic exposure-to-sigma kinetics model or inspection credit. Printed SI evaluation-temperature grid -46 to 649 C; no extrapolation. Linear interpolation is caller-selected.

damage/temper-j-factor.title: Temper embrittlement composition J factor
limitations: Inputs are numerical weight percentages, not 0-1 fractions. Correlation for 2.25Cr-1Mo/3Cr-1Mo susceptibility; factor alone does not determine DF. Printed eq (2.90) has an unresolved 10^4 exponent; automatic J-to-temperature-shift conversion is not enabled.

damage/temper-xbar.title: Temper embrittlement composition X-bar factor
limitations: Inputs are numerical weight percentages, not fractions or ppm. Owner qualifies applicability to 1.25Cr-0.5Mo/1Cr-0.5Mo alloys.

damage/temper-xbar-shift.title: X-bar long-term FATT temperature shift
limitations: Equation output is a Celsius temperature difference, hence numerically K, per §21.7. Negative predicted shifts are rejected; no implicit zero clipping. Long-term empirical relation; material and exposure applicability require owner qualification.

damage/temper-generation-shift.title: Fabrication-era conservative FATT shift
limitations: Printed paired C/F shifts are inconsistent as temperature differences. Caller must choose printed_C or printed_F_difference_converted explicitly; this choice is preserved in output. The text says after 1988 and the preceding band ends 1987: year 1988 is rejected. No pre-1965 rule.

damage/temper-embrittlement.title: Low-alloy temper embrittlement damage factor
limitations: Owner qualifies susceptible alloy/exposure and minimum pressurization temperature. Uses supplied measured/qualified delta-FATT; no automatic ambiguous SCE or J-factor shift. No service-experience reduction or inspection credit is specified in §21 STEP 6, and neither is applied. US reference table converted to SI, printed SI base-DF grids; no extrapolation.

bundle/weibayes-history.title: Fixed-shape bundle Weibayes life estimate
limitations: At least two matched life records and one failure required; failures and right-censored suspensions enter the powered exposure sum. Owner qualifies unchanged design/material/service and externally selected shape. Does not fit shape, perform database matching, goodness-of-fit or Fisher confidence bounds.

bundle/condition-update.title: Add inspection-predicted bundle failure point
limitations: Adds predicted total life as one additional failure point, including one additional failure in denominator. This is not another right-censored observation. Owner supplies qualified predicted total life; statistical confidence and additional uncertainty are separate.

bundle/thickness-life.title: Inspection-based tube thinning and predicted life
limitations: General corrosion and average tube thickness only. Printed eq (1.72) uses RWT*t_original/rate although RWT is described as remaining wall fraction; a physical threshold extrapolation uses (1-RWT)*t_original/rate. Caller must select basis explicitly. Both agree for the printed 0.5 example. Zero measured loss gives no finite extrapolated life, not a manufactured failure point.

bundle/estimated-life.title: Predicted bundle life from estimated remaining life
limitations: Primitive or utility calculation with no additional clause-specific limitation; caller must qualify API 581 applicability, input basis and engineering use.

bundle/life-extension.title: Effective bundle age after life-extension action
limitations: Owner supplies qualified LEF. Returns effective age rather than imposing a date/day-count convention. Original age is not reset by an ordinary inspection or cleaning; apply only after a qualifying life-extension action.

bundle/consequence.title: Bundle failure or planned replacement financial consequence
limitations: All monetary inputs must share declared currency and price year. Caller explicitly chooses planned or unplanned shutdown duration and environmental cost. No silent historical environmental default or inflation assumption.

bundle/risk.title: Bundle unreliability-weighted consequence
limitations: Weibull cumulative probability times consequence. Despite source annual-risk terminology, this product is a probability-weighted monetary amount at age, not an instantaneous annual failure-frequency risk. No confidence-bound/inspection-uncertainty shift is inferred.

bundle/target-age.title: Bundle age at owner probability-weighted risk target
limitations: Uses an explicitly supplied target on the same probability-weighted consequence basis as bundle/risk. Target >= consequence has no finite crossing. Owner must supply any confidence-bound/uncertainty-adjusted Weibull parameters; raw parameters are not automatically treated as 90% LBC.

bundle/deferral-decision.title: Conditional incremental risk and inspection/replacement economics
limitations: Conditioned on survival to first turnaround; uses survival ratio, not the difference of unconditional CDFs. Source prose reverses action-cost inequality; explicit eqs (1.83)-(1.84) are followed: action cost*(1+ROR) < EIR. Both economic flags may be true; this is not an exclusive inspection plan.

bundle/replacement-optimization.title: Bundle planned-replacement grid cost optimization
limitations: Source right-endpoint failure-life integration on uniform grid; days/year=365.24. Global minimum is over supplied finite grid only, not an unbounded certified optimum. Boundary minima are flagged. No confidence bounds, cost inflation or automatic inspection effects. Grid limited to 10000 points.

bundle/material-factor.title: Bundle replacement material cost factor
limitations: Historical generic bundle factors, not current quotations or the fixed-equipment material factors. Caller may supply a different qualified factor directly to replacement-cost.

bundle/replacement-cost.title: Volume/material-scaled bundle replacement cost
limitations: Printed reference volume 3.016 m3 and default reference quote USD22000. Reference quote date is not inferred from edition year; caller supplies qualified price-index multiplier and FX to declared output price year/currency. This is a size/material estimate, not a vendor quote.

bundle/life-extension-factor.title: Suggested bundle life-extension action factor

ferrules_for_localized_tube_end_damage.title: Ferrules For Localized Tube End Damage

references: Part 1 Table8.5 Effects of Bundle Life Extension Methods; PDF p121
limitations: This is the second table numbered8.5; inspection uncertainty is a different table. Suggested values need owner qualification. Spare factor .5 assumes unknown condition. Ferrules .75 only for localized tube-end erosion/corrosion/impingement protection.

bundle/categories.title: Bundle probability and financial consequence categories
limitations: Uses displayed probability and financial-USD thresholds, not inconsistent DF/area footnotes. Caller explicitly declares consequence on printed USD basis; no automatic present-value inflation or FX normalization. Returns categories only; owner risk-color matrix is separate.

prd/default-weibull.title: PRD default Weibull parameters and design modifiers
limitations: Owner selects severity independently for FAIL and LEAK. Uses printed rounded pilot-operated eta (33.7,8.0,3.5), not another division of these entries. Closed-system factor .75 applies only to conventional FAIL; soft-seat factor 1.25 only to conventional/balanced LEAK. Environmental and inspection adjustments are separate.

prd/environment-factor.title: PRD environmental characteristic-life modifier
limitations: Products of applicable modifiers. LEAK excessive-actuation modifier is not reapplied when operating-ratio modifier applies (Table7.6 note2). Pilot high-ratio exception must be explicitly qualified. Printed strict 200<T<500 F and T>500 F leave exactly 500 F unresolved for LEAK; it is rejected. FAIL does not use temperature/ratio/vibration/cyclic factors.

prd/set-pressure-factor.title: PRD leakage set-pressure probability modifier
limitations: Pressure ratio supplied on a consistent pressure basis. Applies to leakage probability after Weibull evaluation, not to eta. Rupture-disk factor=1.

prd/overpressure-factor.title: PRD fail-to-open overpressure modifier
limitations: Primitive or utility calculation with no additional clause-specific limitation; caller must qualify API 581 applicability, input basis and engineering use.

prd/demand-rate.title: PRD case and total demand rates
limitations: Reduction factor is the residual fraction multiplying initiating frequency, not its reciprocal. Owner qualifies independent demand cases and LOPA credits; defaults/automatic relief-design basis are not inferred.

prd/inspection-update.title: PRD single inspection characteristic-life update
limitations: Implements printed eq (1.20), including CF_pass in its second term. Ineffective tests and durations<1 year get no update. Pass/no-leak cannot reduce eta, fail/leak cannot increase eta. Plugged piping overrides pass to fail. Caller sequences records and handles overhaul/as-new date and invalidation after design change. Invalid weighted probability is rejected, not clipped.

prd/protected-equipment.title: Protected equipment overpressure loss-of-containment model
limitations: Uses normal damage-adjusted frequency at pressure<=MAWP; above MAWP applies printed exponential and caps source-model probability at1. Source mixes annual-frequency/probability terms; returned source_model_loc_probability follows the published model, not a Poisson conversion. Caller supplies DF at evaluation time and all four GFF holes.

prd/fail-frequency.title: PRD fail-to-open loss-of-containment scenario frequency
limitations: One demand case: multiplies scenario-adjusted POFOD, demand rate and protected-equipment LOC model probability. Sum only justified distinct scenarios; dependencies and common-cause effects require owner analysis.

prd/base-reliability.title: PRD default/design/environment/scenario probability
limitations: Uninspected/default reliability path only; no implicit inspection history. Computes cumulative Weibull probability at age and applies Fop for FAIL or Fset for LEAK. LEAK result is not automatically reinterpreted as an instantaneous annual frequency. Caller supplies qualified severity, environmental and pressure inputs.

prd/leakage-rates.title: PRD minor/moderate/combined/stuck-open leakage rates

mild_moderate_equation_rate_kg_s.title: Mild Moderate Equation Rate Kg S

limitations: Capacity must be evaluated at normal operating conditions, not silently copied from a relief-condition rating. Eq(1.40) uses 1% for combined mild/moderate; Table7.15 uses 1% minor and 10% moderate. Both are returned explicitly. API520 capacity sizing is not implemented here.

prd/leakage-duration.title: PRD size/discharge leakage duration
limitations: NPS is a nominal inlet designation, not a measured diameter in metres. Table duration days are converted exactly to seconds (including printed .33 days). Stuck-open duration uses exact30 minutes=1800s, not rounded .021 days.

prd/inventory-loss-factor.title: PRD residual inventory loss factor after recovery
limitations: Factor Fr multiplies lost-inventory cost: closed system0, flare with recovery .5, otherwise1. It does not reduce physical leaked mass or environmental/repair/production costs.

prd/inventory-loss.title: PRD leakage inventory mass and financial loss
limitations: SI mass rate kg/s times seconds replaces source hourly-rate/day factor24. Fluid value must correspond to the protected equipment at the PRD location. Constant supplied operating-capacity leak; no automatic finite inventory/supply limit.

prd/repair-cost.title: PRD reference repair quote adjusted to declared price basis
limitations: Printed reference USD1000 below NPS6, USD2000 at/above NPS6. Price quote year is not inferred from edition year; explicit owner-qualified price index and FX required. Actual work-order cost is preferred and can be supplied directly to leakage-consequence.

prd/production-loss.title: PRD leakage shutdown production loss

mild_leak_tolerated_or_online_repair.title: Mild Leak Tolerated Or Online Repair

limitations: Mild/moderate leak tolerated or isolated/repaired online has zero production loss. Stuck-open case uses shutdown loss per eq(1.47). Caller supplies actual shutdown duration and production margin, including any qualified zero-duration repair.

prd/leakage-consequence.title: PRD two/three-case leakage financial consequence

mild_leak_tolerated_or_online_repair.title: Mild Leak Tolerated Or Online Repair

limitations: Caller explicitly selects two_case_equations (.9 at1% capacity + .1 stuck at25%) or three_case_table_7_15 (.5 at1%, .4 at10%, .1 at25%) because source rates conflict. Non-stuck cases share Table7.14 duration. Environmental and repair costs are common conditional case costs as printed. All monetary inputs share declared currency/year; no automatic price-year inference or supply/inventory cap.

prd/multiple-device-pressure.title: Multiple PRD area-based protected-equipment pressure adjustment

unreduced_pressure_for_fop_pa_gauge.title: Unreduced Pressure For Fop Pa Gauge

limitations: Total installed area includes analyzed PRD. Fa=max(.25,sqrt(Aprd/Atotal)). Reduced pressure is used for protected-equipment LOC and consequence calculations only; original scenario pressure must be retained for Fop (PRD POFOD). Source square-root approximation is not an independent parallel-failure probability or a capacity-design verification.

prd/fail-risk.title: PRD fail-to-open case sum and protected-equipment maximum risk
limitations: Within each protected item, sum distinct demand-case frequency*conditional consequence. Then take maximum across protected items as prescribed, not their sum. Caller supplies qualified case frequencies and pressure-dependent COF; currency/year must be common.

prd/leakage-risk.title: PRD leakage consequence weighted by declared probability/frequency basis
limitations: Source multiplies leakage Weibull cumulative probability by consequence but uses annual-risk terminology. Basis must be explicit: source_cumulative_probability gives monetary probability-weighted consequence; annual_frequency requires an independently qualified annual event frequency. No silent CDF annualization.

prd/total-risk.title: PRD combined risk with explicit dimensional basis
limitations: Annual leakage-frequency basis permits an annual total. Source cumulative-probability basis reproduces printed addition only as source_total_risk_index and leaves annual_financial_risk unset, because summands have inconsistent dimensions. Source index must not be presented as a certified monetary annual rate.

prd/risk-assessment.title: Compose protected-item fail risk and PRD leakage risk
limitations: Integration over supplied case frequencies, protected-item conditional consequences and leakage measure/consequence. It does not automatically derive complete relief design or COF. Fail risk takes max across protected items. Cumulative leakage basis yields source index only; annual total requires qualified leakage annual frequency.

prd/service-age.title: PRD as-new service age and valid-history start boundary
limitations: Overhaul/replacement reset effective age; test alone does not. Replacement/design change invalidate earlier parameter-updating history. Inspection update window starts at later of last as-new reset and parameter-history validity boundary per §7.2.6 STEP6.4. Design change alone does not assert an as-new condition. Dates/age only, not automatic test/eta updating or new-curve qualification. Default365.25-day year is an explicit engineering calendar convention, not a claimed source mandate. Same-day ordered events are allowed.

level1/type1-flammable-area.title: Type1 single-effect flammable consequence area
limitations: Ten Type1 flammable fluids. Caller selects phase, release type and AINL/AIL branch; no Type0 IC or AIT blending. Instantaneous energy correction follows STEP8.2 and §4.8.4. Blank cells are rejected, printed zero retained. Equipment/personnel are callable separately when only one source cell exists.

level1/type1-flammable-consequence.title: Type1 equipment and personnel flammable areas
limitations: Unblended Type1 branch selected explicitly by caller. Requires populated equipment and personnel cells; use type1-flammable-area to query just one effect. Energy/mitigation applied once; coefficients already incorporate event probabilities.

level1/release-to-type1-flammable.title: Compose controlled release and Type1 flammable consequence
limitations: Single qualified hole. Uses gas/liquid source, inventory and detection/isolation duration; Type1 phase/AIT branch is caller-qualified. No Type0 blending. Toxic/financial/other-hole aggregation remain separate composable functions.

properties/water-partial-pressure.title: Water partial pressure for radiation attenuation
references: Part3 eq(3.141), Annex3.B C20/C21; PDF pp552,648
limitations: Uses printed1.013kPa,5328K and14.4114. RH in this equation is percent; public fraction is multiplied by100. Rejects pressure above declared ambient pressure. Empirical ambient correlation, not a general steam/ice or cryogenic property solver.

effects/atmospheric-transmissivity.title: Water-vapor thermal-radiation transmissivity
references: Part3 eq(3.140), Annex3.B C19; PDF pp552,648
limitations: Equation exponent-.09 and C19=1.085 with pressure in kPa. Annex dimensional exponent.092 differs; equation exponent followed. Capped at physical maximum1. At zero water pressure uses limiting tau=1 and reports no finite uncapped value.

effects/pool-mixture-burning-rate.title: Mole-weighted liquid-mixture pool burning rate
limitations: Source mole-fraction weighting of supplied component burning rates; not a mixture thermodynamic or unignited evaporation model. Fractions must sum to1 and are not silently normalized.

effects/pool-flame-geometry.title: Thomas pool flame length and wind tilt
limitations: Air density enters Thomas length; vapor density enters nondimensional wind (not interchangeable). Wind must be qualified at source reference height6ft above grade. Printed powers.67,.333,-.21 followed. No automatic wind-height conversion or LH2 validation.

effects/pool-surface-emissive-power.title: Pool flame surface emissive power
limitations: Surface emissive power W/m2, not total radiated power W. Uses printed cylindrical side-plus-top area2*pi*R*L+pi*R^2. Uniform emissive surface; no smoke shielding or fuel-specific emissivity model.

effects/pool-cylinder-view-factor.title: Pool cylinder vertical/horizontal/maximum view factors
limitations: Printed2016 Fv has atan(q), not atan(sqrt(q)), and numerator2Y(1+sin(theta)), not2Y(1+Xsin(theta)). api581_printed reproduces these; geometry_checked makes the two explicit changes verified against independent side-surface integration. Not an authorized standard erratum. Requires Y>1+Xsin(theta), outside downwind flame projection. Ground target in tilt plane; uniform side emission. Physical-range flag must be checked before flux use.

effects/pool-radiation-flux.title: Pool thermal radiation at a specified surface separation
limitations: Source nomenclature defines xs from flame surface, but printed Y=xs/R conflicts with axis-distance geometry. Caller selects printed_surface_ratio (Y=xs/R) or surface_to_axis (Y=(xs+R)/R). Atmospheric path always uses surface separation. Invalid physical view factors are rejected; no automatic formula fallback.

effects/pool-fire-distance.title: Pool radiation threshold separation and consequence area
limitations: Assumes decreasing flux outside downwind flame envelope. Solves only within supplied maximum distance; no implicit expansion or far-field substitution. If flux already below limit at domain boundary, returns conservative flame-envelope separation and boundary status, not a claimed threshold crossing. Area always pi*(surface_distance+pool_radius)^2. Printed formula/geometry and distance convention are explicit; no validated LH2 applicability.

effects/pool-fire-consequence.title: Compose burning, pool size, flame and radiation consequence areas
limitations: Single pool/event only; no ignition/event or hole weighting. Qualified liquid rainout rate/mass supplied; inventory input is liquid mass, not automatic substitution of ambiguous frac_ro in printed eq(3.132). Site limit mandatory. Explicit printed/geometry_checked and distance choices; source-view-factor discrepancies are not silently corrected. Uniform plume model, no smoke/terrain/flame-impingement or LH2-specific validation.

inspection/effectiveness-category.title: API 581 Annex 2.C common inspection effectiveness category metadata
limitations: Returns the common qualitative category metadata only. It does not decide whether a particular NDE method satisfies a mechanism-specific table; use the dedicated inspection effectiveness APIs for that decision.
Category E means ineffective or insufficiently evidenced for inspection credit. A-D labels are qualitative and do not by themselves define a numeric damage-factor reduction.

inspection/thinning-effectiveness.title: API 581 Annex 2.C.8 thinning inspection effectiveness category
limitations: Implements the printed general/local thinning percentage examples only. It classifies inspection effectiveness; it does not calculate inspection uncertainty, PoF, damage factor or inspection credit.

The caller must qualify inspection quality, CML/location selection and technique effectiveness. A failed qualification returns E rather than manufacturing credit. Thresholds follow the table's percentage bands; ambiguous technique descriptions are not inferred.

inspection/scc-effectiveness.title: API 581 Annex 2.C.9 stress-corrosion-cracking inspection effectiveness category
limitations: Implements the common percentage bands in the SCC example tables. It classifies inspection effectiveness only; it does not calculate SCC susceptibility, inspection uncertainty, PoF or damage factor.

For CLSCC/PTA the source provides no non-intrusive A-level technique; this API returns E unless a lower category threshold is met. Caller must qualify inspection quality, suspect-area definition and indication follow-up.

inspection/external-effectiveness.title: API 581 Annex 2.C.10 external-damage inspection effectiveness category
limitations: Implements the printed external-corrosion, external CLSCC, CUI and CUI-CLSCC percentage examples. It classifies inspection effectiveness only and does not calculate external damage factor or inspection uncertainty.
CUI-CLSCC/non-removed insulation has no source technique for A-D and therefore remains E. Caller must qualify exposed/suspect area definition, inspection quality and follow-up.

inspection/buried-effectiveness.title: API 581 Annex 2.C.7 buried-component inspection effectiveness category

partial_smart_pig_or_specialized_crawler.title: Partial Smart Pig Or Specialized Crawler

references: Part 2 Annex C §2.C.7.1-§2.C.7.2, Table 2.C.7.1; PDF pp452-453
limitations: Classifies the example intrusive/non-intrusive evidence bundles in Table 2.C.7.1. It does not infer corrosion rate, cathodic-protection adequacy, soil corrosivity, PoF or damage factor.

The caller must qualify the evidence flags and coverage. A missing qualification basis or low inspection quality returns E; partial excavation and non-intrusive evidence are not silently promoted to full coverage.

inspection/prd-effectiveness.title: API 581 Annex 2.C.3 pressure-relief-device inspection effectiveness category
references: Part 2 Annex C §2.C.3-§2.C.3.1, Table 2.C.3.1; PDF pp445-446
limitations: Implements the Table 2.C.3.1 evidence examples. It classifies inspection effectiveness only and does not calculate PRD failure frequency, service-age factor, set-pressure factor or leak consequence.
Rupture-disk A-level inspection is explicitly unavailable in the source table. Missing qualification basis or incomplete evidence returns E rather than an optimistic category.

inspection/lining-effectiveness.title: API 581 Annex 2.C.6 non-metallic lining inspection effectiveness category
references: Part 2 Annex C §2.C.6.1-§2.C.6.2, Table 2.C.6.1; PDF pp451-452
limitations: Implements the example percentage bands for corrosion-resistant non-metallic liners. The source states this inspection effectiveness is not currently used in the lining damage factor calculation; this API does not change that rule.
Non-intrusive A-level inspection is explicitly unavailable in the source table. Inspection quality, suspect-area definition and test suitability remain owner-qualified inputs.

inspection/tube-bundle-uncertainty.title: API 581 Annex 2.C.4.1 default tube-bundle inspection uncertainty
limitations: Returns the recommended additional-uncertainty percentage only: A=5%, B=10%, C=20%, D=30%, E=50%. It does not shift a Weibull curve or calculate tube-bundle PoF by itself.
The source says tube-bundle LoIE tables are owner-user defined; the category and basis remain caller-qualified and must not be inferred from an NDE name alone.

inspection/ast-effectiveness.title: API 581 Annex 2.C.5 atmospheric storage tank inspection effectiveness category
limitations: Implements the example AST shell-internal, shell-external and tank-bottom evidence bands. It does not calculate tank corrosion rate, minimum thickness, PoF or financial consequence.

The caller must select the correct side and qualify inspection quality, exposed/suspect area and API 653/NDE interpretation. Inputs from multiple sides are not silently combined into a higher category.

effects/fireball-mass.title: Flammable mass available to a rupture fireball
limitations: Mass fraction of available release inventory, not mole fraction or dispersion cloud mass. Instantaneous rupture applicability must be established by caller.

effects/fireball-view-factor.title: Fireball spherical radiation view factor
limitations: Explicit basis required: api581_printed follows eqs(3.165)-(3.166), C=.5*hypot(D,xs), F=D^2/(D^2+xs^2), without using H=.75D. elevated_sphere_maximum is a separately identified geometric interpretation: grade receiver at horizontal radius xs, sphere center H=.75D, receiver plane normal facing the center, F=(D/(2*hypot(H,xs)))^2. It is not an authorized erratum.

effects/fireball-radiation-flux.title: Fireball received thermal radiation
limitations: Explicit basis required: api581_printed follows eqs(3.165)-(3.166), C=.5*hypot(D,xs), F=D^2/(D^2+xs^2), without using H=.75D. elevated_sphere_maximum is a separately identified geometric interpretation: grade receiver at horizontal radius xs, sphere center H=.75D, receiver plane normal facing the center, F=(D/(2*hypot(H,xs)))^2. It is not an authorized erratum.

Printed basis uses nominal xs for atmospheric attenuation. Elevated sphere uses center-to-receiver distance minus radius. Zero printed path uses capped limiting transmissivity1. No flame contact or LH2-specific validation.

effects/fireball-distance.title: Fireball thermal threshold distance and area
limitations: Explicit basis required: api581_printed follows eqs(3.165)-(3.166), C=.5*hypot(D,xs), F=D^2/(D^2+xs^2), without using H=.75D. elevated_sphere_maximum is a separately identified geometric interpretation: grade receiver at horizontal radius xs, sphere center H=.75D, receiver plane normal facing the center, F=(D/(2*hypot(H,xs)))^2. It is not an authorized erratum.

Monotone spherical flux solution within caller maximum distance; no automatic bracket expansion. Returns safe upper bracket, with error bounded by distance_tolerance_m. Area=pi*distance^2 per printed equations; elevated-sphere distance is horizontal radius. If origin is below threshold returns zero area and no claimed threshold root.

effects/fireball-consequence.title: Rupture fireball radiation consequence chain
limitations: Explicit basis required: api581_printed follows eqs(3.165)-(3.166), C=.5*hypot(D,xs), F=D^2/(D^2+xs^2), without using H=.75D. elevated_sphere_maximum is a separately identified geometric interpretation: grade receiver at horizontal radius xs, sphere center H=.75D, receiver plane normal facing the center, F=(D/(2*hypot(H,xs)))^2. It is not an authorized erratum.

Instantaneous rupture only. Caller qualifies inventory, combustion heat, and burst pressure: normal operating pressure for normal rupture or likely elevated pressure for PRD failure. Pressure correlation giving radiative fraction above1 is rejected. Constant or water-vapor atmospheric model is explicit. No ignition probability weighting, duration-dose injury model, or LH2 validation.

effects/vce-scaled-distance.title: Hopkinson TNT scaled distance
references: Part3 eq(3.171), Annex3.B C27=1; PDF pp558,648

release/bleve-flashed-amount.title: Flashed liquid mass and amount for BLEVE
references: Part3 STEP10.3(1), nomenclature nv/MW; PDF pp571,576
limitations: Caller supplies liquid flash mass fraction qualified at atmospheric release; this is not an EOS/isenthalpic flash solver. Amount is kmol (source kg-mol), not mol. Only stored liquid is counted; pre-existing vapor is handled separately.

effects/bleve-liquid-tnt.title: Flashed-liquid BLEVE expansion energy and TNT equivalent
references: Part3 eq(3.195), Annex3.B C30; PDF pp569,648; nv/R units PDF576,578
limitations: Uses printed C30=9.76e-8 kg/J and R=8314 J/(kmol*K), nv in kmol, storage temperature K, natural log of absolute burst/ambient pressure. Does not infer flash amount from fluid properties. Vapor-space contribution is excluded and must be added separately for two-phase contents. No combustion/fireball energy included.

effects/physical-explosion-consequence.title: Gas-vessel rupture blast consequence
limitations: Only rupture hole produces blast area; other holes return not_rupture with zero event equivalent and area while retaining potential inventory rupture energy. Personnel default is probit5 (50% building collapse), equipment default34500Pa. Reuses caller-qualified TNT fit domain; no extrapolation, direct lethality, fragmentation or LH2 validation.

effects/bleve-consequence.title: Liquid/two-phase BLEVE blast consequence
limitations: Sums liquid and pre-existing vapor TNT equivalents using their distinct printed C30/C29 coefficients. Shared absolute burst/ambient pressure; vapor volume must exclude liquid, flashed amount must exclude pre-existing vapor. No automatic EOS, superheat applicability, fireball or combustion calculation. Only rupture produces blast area. Caller-qualified fit domain and building-collapse proxy limits apply; LH2 validation outstanding.

consequence/level2-nfnt-case.title: Level2 NFNT maximum areas and non-ignition weighting
limitations: Inputs are event-conditional unweighted areas. Uses maximum, not sum, then applies non-ignition probability once. Physical/BLEVE areas must be zero for non-rupture holes. Steam/chemical area can be supplied by Level1 NFNT calculation. This does not infer event-tree probabilities.

consequence/level2-nfnt-summary.title: Four-hole Level2 NFNT GFF-weighted final areas
limitations: Requires small,medium,large,rupture once each, including zero-frequency holes. Weights per-case non-ignition-adjusted maximum areas by supplied generic frequencies, not DF-adjusted failure frequencies. No annual risk or financial consequence is computed by this area average.

release/level2-toxic-duration.title: Level2 toxic release duration bound
limitations: Minimum of3600s, full inventory/full mixture rate, detection/isolation duration. Do not divide full inventory by toxic-component rate. Constant-rate source approximation; no transient depressurization. Release duration is not automatically receptor exposure duration.

consequence/toxic-mixture-limit.title: Homogeneous mixture cloud toxic concentration criterion
limitations: Divides pure-component ppm criterion by toxic mole fraction, not mass fraction. Applies when dispersion concentration represents entire homogeneous mixture using full release rate. Species-resolved concentration must not be divided again. Zero mole fraction means absent component; no finite modified criterion is returned.

consequence/level2-toxic-case.title: Selected toxic cloud footprints to conditional toxic consequence
limitations: Caller supplies one chosen criterion and qualified footprint per toxic component. Criteria hierarchy: probit/LC50, then ERPG3/AEGL3/TEEL3, then IDLH/EPA endpoint. Selection within a tier is caller-qualified, not maximum across incomparable exposure criteria. Takes largest component area and applies non-ignition probability once; equipment toxic damage area is0. Does not run dispersion or sum overlapping clouds.

consequence/level2-toxic-summary.title: Four-hole GFF-weighted Level2 toxic consequence
limitations: Requires all four canonical holes once. Takes component maximum and non-ignition weighting within each hole, then generic-frequency average. No DF-adjusted frequency substitution or financial/individual-risk computation. Cloud footprints and selected exposure criteria remain externally qualified inputs.

level2/correlated-jet-pool.title: One immediate-ignition branch with max(jet,pool) area
references: Part3 Figure5.3 two-phase continuous immediate branch; PDF p586; eqs(3.176)-(3.177)
limitations: One branch probability applies to maximum jet/pool area, separately for equipment and personnel. Do not treat jet and pool as two independent terminal probabilities or sum their areas. Source footprints supplied and qualified externally; no geometric union or simultaneous-fire radiation solver.

level2/flammable-case.title: Flammable areas with optional correlated immediate branch
limitations: Requires pool,jet,fireball,VCE,flash outcomes exactly once, including explicit zero branches. Together with optional correlated_jet_pool and non-ignition probabilities they sum to1. Raw areas weighted once. Correlated max(jet,pool) only for continuous leakage; separate jet/pool branches must be zero. Fireball defaults to instantaneous rupture-only text; explicit figure53_instantaneous also permits figure5.3 instantaneous leakage. Caller qualifies tree/area sources.

level2/final-area.title: Final Level2 component/personnel consequence areas
limitations: Inputs must already be event- and hole-weighted on a common basis. Equipment=flammable+NFNT; personnel=flammable+max(toxic,NFNT); final=max(equipment,personnel). Safe-event areas are0. Do not replace with Level1 maximum over all mechanisms or apply non-ignition probability twice.

level2/consequence-summary.title: GFF mechanism averages followed by Level2 final selection
limitations: All four holes required. Input mechanism areas already include event/non-ignition probabilities. GFF averages are formed separately before final non-ignition maximum. Averaging per-hole maxima generally gives a different result. No DF-adjusted frequencies as GFF weights.

level2/scenario-consequence.title: One-hole flammable/toxic/NFNT mechanism consequences
limitations: Supplied terminal probabilities and raw event/footprint areas; no release or dispersion calculation is inferred. One shared non-ignition probability drives toxic and NFNT. Empty toxic list requires explicit not_applicable with basis. Outputs remain separate mechanisms; final selection is after hole weighting.

level2/scenario-summary.title: Four raw event scenarios to final Level2 consequence areas
limitations: Caller-qualified event probabilities and raw event/dispersion areas for all four holes. Composes conditional mechanisms, separate GFF averages, flammable addition and non-ignition maximum. Does not run thermodynamics, dispersion or applicability inference.

release/level2-source-partition.title: Pool/jet/vapor/aerosol mass and rate partition
limitations: Adjusted total rate and released mass must be qualified after detection/isolation and inventory limits. Pool+jet and jet-vapor+jet-liquid conserve mass. release/flammable-phase-rates.title: Flammable total/liquid/vapor rates for ignition
limitations: Flash fraction supplied by qualified thermodynamics. Phase liquid rate is not pool rainout rate; aerosol/rainout partition is separate. Flammable mass fraction, not mole fraction, multiplies total adjusted rate.

events/ambient-ignition.title: Flash-point/rate ambient ignition correlation
limitations: Printed C12=1.8 converts Kelvin flash point to Rankine; C4B=2.205 converts capped kg/s to lb/s inside natural log. Uses C5=25.2kg/s even though adjacent text also says25.22. events/probability-temperature.title: Reference-to-AIT probability interpolation
limitations: Printed C16=30.89K and US70R conflict with ambient-temperature discussion; no silent conversion to70F. Required basis chooses literal C16 or a caller-qualified reference. events/conditional-table.title: Table5.3 conditional event probabilities
limitations: Historical expert-opinion defaults by phase/release type. Immediate probability at reference, not automatically at current storage temperature. VCE and flash columns are conditional on delayed ignition, not unconditional outcomes.

events/two-phase-probability.title: Explicit-basis liquid/vapor conditional probability mixing
limitations: Printed equations weight LIQUID by flash fraction and VAPOR by its complement, despite flash-as-vapor wording. Literal and separately qualified vapor weighting are explicit alternatives; neither is silently selected or asserted as an erratum. Inputs must be probabilities of the same conditional quantity. No complete two-phase terminal tree or correlated max(jet,pool) consequence representation here.

events/single-phase-tree.title: Single-phase terminal paths from Figures5.3/5.4
references: Part3 Figures5.3/5.4; PDF pp586-587; conflicting example eq(3.125) PDF549

events/single-phase-ignition.title: Rate/flash-point/temperature to single-phase terminal probabilities
limitations: Composes supplied phase flammable rate and qualified flash point, printed or qualified temperature reference, AIT maximum and Table5.3. events/fireball-given-immediate.title: Fireball conditional applicability from text or figure basis
limitations: Conditional on immediate ignition. Text basis requires instantaneous rupture of vapor/two-phase; explicit figure53 basis also allows instantaneous leakage. Liquid and continuous cases give0. Correlation does not establish thermal-model applicability or certify leakage fireballs.

events/two-phase-tree.title: Two-phase figure paths including one correlated jet/pool event

events/two-phase-ignition.title: Phase rates and ignition correlations to two-phase terminal paths

damage/groundwater-tks.title: Groundwater Total Key Species on a qualified common concentration basis
limitations: Sum of seven explicitly supplied species concentrations, public mg/L on a qualified common analytical basis. No missing species assumed zero, molar/mass conversion, speciation or charge balance. Inputs must not double-count total inorganic carbon or report nitrogen/sulfur equivalents without conversion qualification. Source supplies no TKS thresholds or TKS-to-corrosion-rate equation; no automatic corrosivity or corrosion rate inferred.

damage/groundwater-rate-classification.title: Groundwater steel corrosivity category from supplied corrosion rate
limitations: Classifies a supplied steel corrosion rate, not TKS. Printed SI limits.03/.25/1.27mm/year differ from1/10/50mpy converted exactly. Explicit unit basis required. The medium/high shared.25mm/year or10mpy endpoint needs explicit lower/higher severity policy. Low is strictly below first threshold; very high strictly above last. No material-specific rate prediction, treatment credit or degradation immunity.

damage/groundwater-assessment.title: Qualified groundwater chemistry and externally established steel corrosion rate
limitations: Competent water-corrosivity specialist must establish the steel corrosion rate independently. TKS is reported alongside that rate, never used to invent source cutoffs or a rate regression. No groundwater-specific quantitative rate equation is provided by the standard. Chemistry, material and specialist qualifications are supplied, not independently verified.

damage/groundwater-thinning-assessment.title: Qualified groundwater rate through non-AST unclad thinning
limitations: Same externally qualified groundwater rate drives loss and non-AST unclad thinning; general/local inspection and steel applicability require explicit basis. No automatic pitting multiplier, TKS-derived rate, MIC/deposit exclusions or treatment credit. Monitoring row must be other; no borrowed acid/sour-water credits. Qualified experience replacement remains separately available under Table4.8. No cladding, AST, FFS or all-mechanism assessment.

damage/thinning-rate-selection.title: Measured-first and maximum-mechanism rate with governing thinning type
limitations: Caller supplies all applicable mechanisms for one component, assessed surface and common current-process plan period. Representative measured CML/history rate wins within each mechanism, including explicit zero. Otherwise exactly the supplied calculated/estimated fallback is used; no invented priority between estimated and calculated rates. Rate is maximum across mechanisms, not sum. Local inspection type governs if any applicable mechanism is local, even when its rate is lower. No missing mechanism assumed absent, automatic mechanism screening, CML regression, rate confidence inference or forecast. Long-term current-process representativeness and rate/type provenance require qualification.

damage/thinning-selected-mechanisms.title: Selected multi-mechanism rate through qualified non-AST thinning
limitations: Maximum selected rate drives one common wall/strength baseline; most localized assigned mechanism governs inspection scope. Caller must qualify inspections for that governing type and all applicable loss locations. Generic composition uses other monitoring row with table factor1; mechanism-specific credits cannot be borrowed across mechanisms. Qualified Table4.8 experience replacement is explicit. Custom priors remain supported. No rate summation, multiple-surface loss, all-mechanism DF, AST, cladding, CML history interpretation or whole-asset risk.

damage/thinning-assessment-period.title: Consistent furnished/measured thickness baseline and elapsed period
limitations: Timezone-aware timestamps normalized to UTC. Furnished thickness starts at installation; selected measured thickness starts at its qualified inspection time, requiring high-quality inspection, high-confidence accuracy and reset basis. Year conversion is explicit caller convention, not an API581-mandated constant. No process-change detection, measurement uncertainty correction, automatic reset selection or thickness reconciliation.

damage/thinning-inspection-history.title: Assessment-period inspection eligibility and direct A-D counts
references: Part2 §§4.5.5-4.5.6; Tables4.6,2.C inspection guidance; PDF pp151-152
limitations: Only performed, qualified inspections in the selected period receive A-D counts; E receives no credit. Before-baseline and after-assessment records remain excluded diagnostics. Exact baseline-time inclusion is explicit owner policy; source does not resolve duplicate use of a baseline-setting inspection. End time is included. Duplicate IDs or a baseline inspection ID with conflicting timestamp fail. No automatic NDE effectiveness grading, equivalent-count conversion, geometry/coverage qualification or credit for planned inspections.

damage/thinning-history-assessment.title: Thickness/history/rate selection through period-consistent thinning DF
limitations: Selected baseline derives both wall thickness and elapsed period; eligible dated inspection records derive counts, with independently selected table/custom prior. No competing manually supplied age/counts. Strength baseline must agree with derived wall baseline. Rate-selection common-period and inspection coverage/type qualifications remain external. Generic other monitoring row only, no borrowed mechanism credits. Non-AST unclad scope; no automatic process-change reset, inspection scheduling, cladding or all-mechanism/asset risk.

damage/caustic-screening.title: Caustic cracking material and any-concentration exposure screen
limitations: Carbon/low-alloy steel with caustic at any concentration requires evaluation. Presence includes qualified local/upset/residual exposure; no5wtpct or normal-process-temperature cutoff is used for screening. Screen-out means outside this procedure, not material immunity, zero overall DF or exclusion of other mechanisms.

damage/caustic-figure-susceptibility.title: Qualified caustic graph area through Figure6.2 and crack-history gate
limitations: Figure6.1/6.1M area is independently qualified from actual maximum metal temperature and effective local NaOH concentration. This API routes the area; it does not digitize/interpolate the graph or certify PWHT. Plot concentration0..50wtpct; exactly5wtpct follows the not-less-than5 branch. Heat tracing and steam-out before water flushing follow Figure6.2.

Detected/repaired historical cracking stays High until an adequately effective subsequent clear inspection AND specialist reassignment basis. Stress relief cannot erase that history. Unrepaired cracks require separate FFS and fail explicitly. No automatic stress-relief temperature/hold-time qualification, alloy immunity or local boiling concentration model.

damage/caustic-screened-assessment.title: Caustic screen and Figure6.2 through SCC severity/inspection/age DF
limitations: Material/exposure screen must pass; outside-scope input fails instead of manufacturing DF0. Figure area/PWHT and crack-history/reassignment declarations require qualification. Uses existing caustic SVI, equivalent highest inspection and age escalation unchanged; source ambiguous E/500 cell and counts beyond6 remain unsupported. Inspection coverage and qualifying age are externally established per §6.6.3, not inferred from generic thinning history. No FFS, graph interpolation or all-mechanism risk.

damage/amine-cracking-screening.title: Any-concentration acid-gas-treating amine SCC material screen
limitations: Carbon/low-alloy steel with acid-gas-treating amines in any concentration requires susceptibility evaluation. No concentration, normal-temperature, amine-type, rich-service or PWHT exclusion is inferred. Lean/rich/fresh composition, actual metal temperature, heat tracing, steam-out and other cracking mechanisms require separate evaluation. Screen-out is outside this procedure, not overall immunity or DF0.

damage/amine-cracking-screened-assessmen.title: Screened amine exposure through qualified SCC susceptibility and DF
limitations: Supplied susceptibility must be independently qualified using Figure7.1 or expert assessment; this API does not implement the figure or predict from amine chemistry. Screening must pass; no synthetic zero DF on screen-out. Confirmed cracking forces High; unrepaired cracks require FFS. Inspection grade/count and time since qualifying A/B/C clear/repaired inspection follow section7.6.3 and remain externally qualified. Existing six-equivalent-inspection support is retained; no all-mechanism assessment.

damage/amine-figure-susceptibility.title: Figure7.1 amine cracking susceptibility
limitations: Literal Fahrenheit flowchart thresholds100/140/180F converted exactly to kelvin.100..180 and140..180 include endpoints after the prior >180 test. Both lean/rich exposure routes lean per Table7.1. Other treating amines follow the printed not-MEA/DIPA/not-DEA branch; mixtures spanning groups require independent qualification, not automatic worst-group selection. Actual maximum metal temperature, heat tracing, steam-out before flushing and effective stress relief require qualification. Confirmed cracks forceHigh before stress relief/composition; unrepaired cracks require FFS. Not an amine corrosion-rate model or automatic chemical speciation/PWHT validation.

damage/amine-figure-assessment.title: Figure7.1 susceptibility through amine SCC DF
limitations: Material/exposure screen, Figure7.1 service declarations and mechanism-specific qualifying inspection age/count require qualification. Reuses existing SVI, equivalent inspection and age escalation, with maximum supported equivalent count6. Rich/fresh none applies only to this amine SCC mechanism, not SSC/HIC/SOHIC or other damage. No whole-component risk, FFS or automatic inspection grading.

damage/ssc-screening.title: SSC carbon/low-alloy steel wet-H2S any-concentration screen
limitations: Evaluate carbon/low-alloy steel whenever both water and H2S are present at any concentration. No1ppm, partial-pressure, pH, temperature, hardness or PWHT cutoff is used to exclude the mechanism at this screen. Presence flags require qualified local/process/upset exposure evidence. Environmental hydrogen severity, cyanide, weld/HAZ Brinnell hardness and heat treatment remain separate susceptibility inputs. Screen-out is outside this procedure, not DF0, FFS acceptance or immunity to other mechanisms.

damage/hic-h2s-screening.title: HIC/SOHIC-H2S steel and wet-H2S any-concentration screen

Carbon and low-alloy steel both enter screening; downstream Table9.3 carbon-steel material/sulfur/product assumptions require independent qualification. PWHT, seamless pipe, low sulfur or low H2S concentration alone do not exclude screening. No automatic SSC/HIC equivalence, SOHIC immunity, blister/crack FFS acceptance or zero DF.

damage/ssc-qualified-susceptibility.title: SSC environment and measured hardness with cyanide susceptibility upgrade

Brinnell must be actually measured, not converted microhardness; PWHT and process chemistry require qualification. Existing source pH gaps and overlapping1000ppm columns fail explicitly. No automatic material applicability or chemical speciation.

damage/ssc-qualified-assessment.title: SSC material/exposure through environment/hardness/cyanide and DF
limitations: Selected material/wet-H2S screen must pass. Reuses existing Table8.2 gaps/overlap guards, Table8.3 actual Brinnell/PWHT susceptibility and one-category cyanide note before crack override. Confirmed cracking forces high; unrepaired cracks require FFS. Caller qualifies mechanism-specific inspection period and coverage. Existing equivalent-count support up to6, age escalation and table DF preserved. No generic thinning-history reuse, FFS or total asset risk.

damage/hic-h2s-qualified-susceptibility.title: HIC/SOHIC-H2S environment/material/cyanide susceptibility

Cyanide note upgrades subsequent susceptibility one category capped high, not environment. Existing pH gaps/1000ppm overlap fail. damage/hic-h2s-monitoring-selection.title: Table9.5 or qualified experience replacement monitoring factor

damage/hic-h2s-qualified-assessment.title: Screened HIC/SOHIC-H2S service through monitoring-adjusted DF
limitations: Carbon-steel integration only, despite broader carbon/low-alloy screening. Known blisters/cracks require explicit repaired or externally qualified FFS disposition and basis; this API performs no FFS. Confirmed cracking must also be declared known. Inspection and age follow section9.6.4, not generic thinning periods. Monitoring is applied once using existing factors1/2/2/4; qualification is mandatory. Existing six-equivalent-inspection and source table guards retained. No whole-asset risk or automatic damage detection.

damage/acscc-screening.title: ACSCC alkaline-water and FCCU feed-change evaluation triggers
limitations: Carbon/low-alloy steel: alkaline water pH>7.5 or reduced-sulfur/increased-nitrogen FCCU feed changes trigger evaluation. Exactly7.5 does not pass the strict water trigger. Feed-change triggers are independent review flags, not proof of carbonate concentration or susceptibility. Water presence requires its qualified pH; absent water must omit pH. No H2S threshold, cyanide exclusion, carbonate estimate, PWHT credit or damage factor is inferred. Outside scope is not overall immunity or zero risk.

damage/acscc-water-susceptibility.title: Qualified numeric water pH to ACSCC carbonate/PWHT susceptibility

limitations: Numeric pH mapped to existing Table10.2 bands. Traditional P/M alkalinity alone is rejected per note1; caller supplies qualified carbonate method. No carbonate inference from total alkalinity, PWHT certification, numeric pH rounding allowance or material applicability.

damage/acscc-qualified-assessment.title: ACSCC screen and common water chemistry through inspection/age DF

damage/pascc-screening.title: PASCC austenitic stainless/nickel alloy sulfur exposure screen

No automatic exclusion for normal-operation dryness, low-carbon/stabilized grade, low operating temperature, alkaline wash or nitrogen purge; shutdown air/moisture and mitigation remain separate evaluation. Material category does not authorize every Table11.2 cell. Screen-out is outside this procedure, not global immunity or zero DF.

damage/pascc-figure-susceptibility.title: PASCC Figure11.1 exposure and qualified downtime protection

properties/mixture-representative-fluid.title: Annex 3.A mole-weighted representative-fluid selection
limitations: Uses Table 4.2M properties and mole-fraction weighting for MW, NBP, density and AIT. Inert/non-consequence-relevant components are excluded as the printed conservative Level 1 rule directs. Hydrocarbon pseudo-components are selected only from the hydrocarbon rows; selection then prioritizes the highest candidate NBP that does not exceed the weighted NBP. references: Part 2 Annex B §1.1-§1.2; Part 2 §4.5.5, PDF pp143-152

Thickness increase is rejected as a measurement/baseline inconsistency rather than silently converted to zero corrosion. The caller must qualify comparable locations, units, dates and measurement quality.

damage/thinning-type.title: API 581 Annex 2.B.1.2 general versus localized thinning designation

limitations: Effective inspection designation takes precedence. If no effective inspection type is supplied, any applicable localized mechanism conservatively selects localized thinning. This API does not screen mechanisms or calculate corrosion rates.
The caller must qualify the mechanism list and inspection effectiveness; an empty inspection list is treated as unknown, not as evidence of general thinning.
